clue.text: Queen performed, getting terrible score

parts.note: performed, as in carried out, means did
a terrible score is nil, zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A monarch sings and the critics give her nought.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage, abandoned by Aeneas.
explanation.definitionFit: Dido is the legendary founding monarch of Carthage in Virgil's Aeneid.

clue.text: Ridiculous not having booze? Old father is upset being kept in

indicators.note: the turned letters are kept inside the other word

parts.note: a dry area or person has no alcohol

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: An absurd teetotal regime, upsetting the old man who is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means laughably small or inadequate, so absurd and deserving scorn.

clue.text: Depression? At end of day get mature drinks!

indicators.note: the other pieces are put at the end of the day abbreviation

parts.note: something mature is old
rums are drinks of the spirit

explanation.surface: Feeling low? At close of day, treat yourself to some aged spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the doldrums means being in a state of low spirits or stagnation.

clue.text: Like very good allocation? That's what's hoped for

parts.note: like, as in similar to, means as
PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
an allocation or share is a ration

explanation.surface: A generous share of supplies is exactly what someone would wish for.
explanation.definitionFit: A hope or ambition is something aimed at and wished for, a goal.

clue.text: Start of symphony with instrument producing note

indicators.note: start of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: the harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: An orchestral opening on a harp produces a musical tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp is a note raised a semitone in pitch.

clue.text: Liaison to break up, leading to loneliness

indicators.note: to break up the letters is to scatter and reassemble them

explanation.surface: An affair ends and the lover is left alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Being isolated means being cut off from others, alone and solitary.

clue.text: Church office Pat polishes after work

indicators.note: after being worked on the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Pat cleans the vestry once the day's job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: The role or office of one of Christ's twelve disciples, a church position.

clue.text: More than one flowering plant is covering upward slope

indicators.note: covering means the outer piece wraps around the other

parts.note: a rise is an upward slope of ground

explanation.surface: Blooms spread over a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: These are flag plants with sword-shaped leaves and showy blooms, plural.

clue.text: Any number fighting, about to leave country

parts.note: N is used in maths for any number

indicators.note: to leave means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: action is fighting in battle
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Troops in combat about to quit a land.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a state or people of a particular land.

clue.text: River not healthy — small flow of water

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps
someone not healthy is ill

explanation.surface: A polluted river reduced to a trickle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rill is a tiny stream or brook, a little runnel of water.

clue.text: Biologist has burden and motion's tricky

parts.note: a tax is a burden or strain imposed on someone

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of the word are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the word motion's supplies its letters including the S

explanation.surface: A scientist weighed down by work finds a debating proposal awkward.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist who classifies living organisms into groups works in biology.

clue.text: Scotch — drink team is into

indicators.note: the team is into the drink, placed within it

parts.note: to sup is to drink, here a noun for a mouthful
a crew is a team, as of rowers

explanation.surface: Whisky: the drink the squad is keen on.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch looks like whisky but is the verb meaning to thwart or wreck a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan is to ruin it, a botch or failure being the noun sense here.

clue.text: Victory over brute whirling with din — for Nimbys opposing it?

indicators.note: in a down clue over places one piece above the next

parts.note: a victory is a win

indicators.note: whirling suggests the letters spin into a new order

explanation.surface: Triumph over noisy turbulence, at least for local protesters against it.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY stands for Not In My Back Yard, someone opposing local development; whirling also describes the blades.
explanation.definitionFit: Local objectors commonly campaign against tall wind-powered generators near their homes.

clue.text: Sort of design company backing trade abroad

indicators.note: backing means supporting, coming behind the other piece
abroad, meaning astray or all over the place, signals the letters scattering

explanation.surface: A firm supporting overseas commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the geometric decorative style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Powerful international organisation that could make Premier moan

indicators.note: the letters given could make the answer when rearranged, hence a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A mighty global body that would have the prime minister complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition playfully treats an ancient empire as an international organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome's ancient realm was a mighty multinational power spanning many lands.

clue.text: Clean-cut love? Lots will get that in marriage!

indicators.note: lots will get the previous pieces put inside them

parts.note: lots means many
trim means neat and clean-cut
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A tidy romance with many guests at the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Matrimony is the state of being wed, wedlock.

clue.text: Drive? A doctor with it will get on, I admitted

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: the letter I is admitted into the other two words

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Determined medic with sex appeal will advance, I confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun means ambition, energy and determination.

clue.text: Observe group around centre of Burnley showing contempt

indicators.note: around means one piece goes around the central letter

parts.note: to observe is to see

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle letter of the word

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of criminals

explanation.surface: Football fans gather round a Burnley player and jeer.
explanation.walkthrough: Burnley is a football town in Lancashire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneering means scornful, expressing disdain through a mocking smile.

clue.text: Pharaoh's word of disapproval, final word clutching symbol of life

indicators.note: the two words hold the symbol between them as if gripping it

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound expressing disapproval
amen ends a prayer, so it is the final word
the ankh is the Egyptian looped cross symbolising life

explanation.surface: An Egyptian king tuts and then says his last word, holding an emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The boy king of Egypt's eighteenth dynasty, whose tomb Carter found in 1922.

clue.text: One-time leader of 14, no hard man

indicators.note: no means the letter is absent from the name

parts.note: Hadrian ruled the empire of 14 across in the second century
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A former ruler without a tough streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrian is a man's given name, so a man.

clue.text: Marksman gets bird on top of roof

parts.note: the snipe is a wading bird with a long bill

indicators.note: top of in a down clue means the first letter

explanation.surface: A gunman shoots a bird perched on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper is a skilled hidden rifleman shooting from cover.

clue.text: Study a king on two classical coins

parts.note: a den is a private study or room
R, for rex, is the Latin abbreviation for king
II is two in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Researching an ancient monarch through a couple of old coins.
explanation.definitionFit: These were silver pieces of ancient Roman money, the plural of denarius.

clue.text: Give notice — there's an object to be won, we hear

indicators.note: we hear indicates the words are spoken, so the sound matters not the spelling

parts.note: something to be won in a contest is a prize

explanation.surface: An announcement that there is a trophy up for grabs.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform or tell someone of something is to make them aware formally.

clue.text: Region encompassing northern battleground

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding the other piece

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: A district around the north becomes a field of conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of combat, a scene of struggle.

clue.text: Politician held in derision, possibly as Archer was?

indicators.note: the politician is held inside the other letters
possibly hints the word could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: MP, member of parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician scorned, perhaps like the disgraced novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, British novelist and Conservative peer, was jailed for perjury in 2001, so Archer is not a bowman here.
explanation.definitionFit: Archer served a prison sentence, so he was locked up in jail.

clue.text: Very small home swamped by motorway

indicators.note: swamped by means surrounded and covered by the other piece

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's major north-south motorway, written MI
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A tiny house drowned out by a nearby motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Mini as an adjective means miniature, tiny or diminutive.

clue.text: Runners may get sent out — perhaps I've grown them from seed

definitions.text: perhaps I've grown them from seed

indicators.note: sent out suggests the letters are dispatched and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener hopes the runner beans he raised will be dispatched to customers.
explanation.walkthrough: Runners suggests athletes, but they are runner beans the grower has raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant grower raises seedlings and young plants for sale.

clue.text: Catch someone grumbling after end of Christmas

indicators.note: after places the grumbler behind the first letter
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: a nag is someone who constantly complains

explanation.surface: A moaner appears once the festive season is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden drawback or catch in a plan.
